title: Can sound travel through water, wood and space?
examples: Does sound travel faster in solids?

explain.say: Try this: put your ear flat on a table and gently tap the far end with a finger. It sounds louder through the table than through the air! So sound can travel through more than just air. Let's sort where sound can go.

draw.text: Can sound travel through water, wood and space?

explain.say: See Sound travels lighting up? Sound travels through air, water, wood, metal and stone. It needs particles to pass the wiggle along, like people passing a ball down a line. Whales sing to each other through the ocean. Have you heard sounds under water at the pool?

Now look at these speed bars. In air, sound travels about 343 metres every second. Which bar is longer, air or water? Water! Sound goes over four times faster in water, because the particles are closer together.

items.label: Steel
items.ask: Does sound travel faster in solids?

explain.say: See the steel bar lighting up, the longest of all? In steel, sound zooms at almost 6000 metres per second. Long ago, people put an ear to the railway track to hear a train coming. Why do you think that worked?

items.label: Steel
items.ask: Does sound travel faster in solids?

explain.say: Last, see Total silence glow. Space is almost empty, with no air to pass the wiggle, so sound cannot travel. Great job, sound explorer! Wow fact: astronauts on a spacewalk talk by radio, because even if they shouted right next to each other, they could not hear a thing.

faq.a: Yes, and it travels over four times faster in water than in air, about 1480 metres per second. Whales and dolphins use sound to talk across long distances.
Sound needs particles to pass on its vibration. Space is almost a vacuum, which means nearly empty, so there is nothing to carry the sound.
asks: Can you hear sound in space?

faq.q: Does sound travel faster in solids?
faq.a: Usually yes. The particles in solids are close and tightly linked, so they pass the vibration on very quickly. Sound moves about 5900 metres per second in steel.
A vacuum is a space with almost no particles in it, not even air. Sound cannot travel through a vacuum.

faq.q: How do astronauts talk in space?
faq.a: They use radios. Radio waves are a kind of light that can travel through empty space, unlike sound.

facts: Approximate speeds of sound: air 343 m/s, water about 1480 m/s, steel about 5900 m/s.
Sound cannot travel through a vacuum because there are no particles to carry the vibration.

quiz.say: Through which of these does sound travel fastest?
quiz.why: Sound travels fastest in solids like steel, about 5900 metres per second.

wrong.0: Air is the slowest of these, about 343 metres per second.
wrong.1: Water is faster than air, but slower than steel.

quiz.say: Why can astronauts not hear each other shout on a spacewalk?
quiz.show: Why can astronauts not hear shouts in space?

options.show: There is no air to carry sound
options.say: There is no air to carry sound

quiz.why: Space has almost no particles, so sound has nothing to travel through.

wrong.0: Even without helmets, there would be no air to carry sound.
wrong.2: Cold does not stop sound; empty space does.
